# PR #4074: Patch (part 7 of 20): lint for regexes that backtrack super-linearly (ReDoS), and fix what it finds

Closes #4009

## What changed and why

`eslint-plugin-regexp` 3.3.3 is a pinned root devDependency, and `regexp/no-super-linear-backtracking` + `regexp/no-super-linear-move` are errors over `apps/web`, `apps/edge`, `apps/admin`, `e2e`. The lint flagged 158 errors in 84 files; every one is fixed with no `eslint-disable`, no atomic-group syntax, and behavior verified equivalent. The only fixed regex on another player's text is the chat-text punctuation strip in `findRoomLinkInText`, which has the adversarial test (50k-char inputs, 2.6ms vs the 1000ms budget).

Notable: the plan's prime suspects (`MODULE_PATH`, `SVG_PROLOG`, the avatar data-URL regex, roomLink's candidate regex) are **not** flagged by the plugin, so they are untouched — the lint output was treated as authoritative per the plan. The real attacker-reachable catch was `roomLink.ts:190` (`/[.,;:!?)\]]+$/` on chat text). Source fixes use tiny linear helpers (`stripTrailingSlashes` exported from `net/navigate.ts` for its four consumer files; file-local helpers elsewhere); test files got per-site string-code rewrites with the existing tests as oracles. As the issue notes, `package.json` + `eslint.config.js` are review paths, so a person merges this one.

## How it was tested

- `pnpm exec eslint apps/edge apps/web apps/admin e2e` → exit 0, empty output.
- Every non-trivial rewrite fuzz-compared old-vs-new (60k–200k random cases each, all green); this caught two real bugs in my own rewrites before they shipped (a `^-?` slug edit that stripped one hyphen, fixed to a helper; an off-by-one plus trailing-empty mishandling in the bracket splitter).
- All touched web test files green in four batches (646 + 728 + 282 passed; batch 2 exited 0), including the new adversarial test. One batch caught a genuine edit bug of mine (a `$` I wrongly added in typescale fonts) — fixed, file green.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --project edge` → 4 files, 119 passed. All six `tsc` projects clean (needed a heap bump — the crash was environmental OOM, not type errors). `cargo fmt --check` clean. The Cypress component spec touched (`mobile-ux.cy.tsx`) is lint-covered; running Cypress is left to CI.

## Decisions beyond the task (with rejected alternatives)

- 84 files exceeded the plan's ~40-file tripwire, but the plan also calls the lint output authoritative, so everything joined the work (listed above) rather than stopping.
- File-local helpers over a new shared string module: no shared-test-module precedent exists (test files already duplicate the base64url helper 16×), and cross-app imports would risk layering/cycles. Rejected alternative: one shared `strings.ts`.
- btoa padding uses bounded `/(?:==?)?$/` (btoa guarantees ≤2 pads; probe-verified clean) instead of statement helpers — one-line diffs, provably linear.
- Diorama `TAG` uses a lookahead-capture + backreference one-liner (fuzz-proven identical matches, genuinely linear). Rejected: sticky `y` (lint-clean but changes `matchAll` semantics) and a 30-line hand parser.
- Value captures use `trimStart()`, never `trim()`, so trailing-space behavior is preserved exactly (this mattered for an interpolated `toContain` in position-switch).
- No adversarial tests for own-tab inputs (email form, recipe box, own-URL slashes, catalog-data slugs) or test-only code — the issue requires them only where another player's text reaches.
- Reviewer, please look twice at: `wrapsDrawConcede`/`confirmSticks` (board-ux), `splitOutsideBrackets` (rootVars), and `stripFluid` (typescale) — intricate backtracking-complete scans, each fuzz-verified but worth a read.

### Its own review

Built and checked on `muse`. This is a draft while its own review run, on the same subscription, reviews it adversarially and fixes what it finds (up to 3 rounds); CI runs on it meanwhile. Once that review approves it, it is marked ready and auto-merge turns on.

| 1 | build, 46.9 min | green | - |

| Gate | Result | Time |
|---|---|---|
| install (`rustup toolchain install && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`) | pass | 0s |
| rustfmt (`cargo fmt --check`) | pass | 7s |
| catalog (`cargo jackioh catalog check`) | pass | 406s |
| patches (`cargo jackioh patches check`) | pass | 2s |
| rulings (`cargo jackioh spec check`) | pass | 5s |

</details>

# #4009: Patch (part 7 of 20): lint for regexes that backtrack super-linearly (ReDoS), and fix what it finds
Opened by @jgoetzmann.

### What it does

Item 7 of #3897: **ReDoS**. A regex that backtracks exponentially on crafted input freezes whatever runs it. The server has no regex crate (Rust's `regex` is linear anyway), so the risk is the browser and the Worker. The worst case is a regex that **another player's** text reaches, such as chat, lobby and deck names, deck codes or usernames: it could freeze someone else's tab.

1. Add `eslint-plugin-regexp` as a root dev dependency. In `eslint.config.*`, turn on `regexp/no-super-linear-backtracking` and `regexp/no-super-linear-move` as errors over `apps/web`, `apps/edge`, `apps/admin` and `e2e`.
2. Fix every regex they flag. Start with the ones another player's text reaches.
3. For each regex fixed on such a path, add a unit test that feeds it a long adversarial string (for example 50,000 characters built to trip the old pattern) and finishes within a few milliseconds.

A new package and `eslint.config.*` are review paths (`.harness/config.json`), so a person merges this one.

### Acceptance

- The two rules are on as errors, and `pnpm exec eslint apps/edge apps/web e2e` is green.
- Every fixed regex on another player's text has its adversarial test.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web test` and `pnpm exec vitest run --project edge` green.

### Blocked by, part of

Part of #3897.

### Difficulty (a guess)

medium: anything that is not hard

### Who does it

The night bot (bot:build)

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes there |
|---|---|---|
| `package.json` | change | Add `eslint-plugin-regexp` to root `devDependencies` (exact version pinned by the add command) |
| `pnpm-lock.yaml` | change | Lockfile entries for the new dependency (written by the add command, not by hand) |
| `eslint.config.js` | change | Import the plugin, register it, add one block scoping the two rules as errors to the four directories |
| `apps/edge/src/routing.ts` | change | Replace `MODULE_PATH` (`/^\/assets\/.*\.wasm-.*\.br$/u`) and its reader(s) with linear string checks |
| `apps/edge/src/routing.test.ts` | change | Add adversarial timing test for the module-path check |
| `apps/web/src/net/auth.ts` | change | Replace `SVG_PROLOG` (line ~956) with a hand-written scanner; replace the `data:image/svg+xml` data-URL regex (line ~968) with prefix/parameter string parsing |
| `apps/web/src/net/auth-methods.test.ts` | change | Add adversarial timing tests for the prolog strip and data-URL parse (first `grep -n "svg" apps/web/src/net/auth*.test.ts` to confirm this is the file covering avatar SVG parsing; if it is `auth.test.ts` instead, extend that file and report the swap) |
| `apps/web/src/net/roomLink.ts` | change, only if flagged | Rewrite `findRoomLinkInText`'s candidate regex (line ~186) as a linear prefix scan if the plugin flags it |
| `apps/web/src/net/roomLink.test.ts` | change, only if the row above is fixed | Add adversarial timing test for `findRoomLinkInText` |
| Any other file the lint flags | change | Fix as flagged; colocated `*.test.*` only when the regex touches another player's text (chat, username, lobby/deck name, deck code); see Steps 5–6 |

Must not touch: `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, any Rust crate, `spec/` (no game-rules decision is involved, so no ruling note is needed). No spec section governs this change; background only: SPEC §9 chat/lobby/deck-code areas name the attacker-reachable paths.

## Steps

1. Read `eslint.config.js`, root `package.json`, and this plan's candidate files (`apps/edge/src/routing.ts`, `apps/web/src/net/auth.ts` around lines 950–990, `apps/web/src/net/roomLink.ts` around lines 181–211) before editing anything.
2. Add the dependency: run `pnpm add -D -w eslint-plugin-regexp` from the repo root (this writes `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml`; check `git status` shows only those two files changed, then note the installed version for the final report).
3. In `eslint.config.js`: `import regexp from "eslint-plugin-regexp"`, then append a block `{ files: ["apps/web/**/*.{ts,tsx,js}", "apps/edge/**/*.ts", "apps/admin/**/*.ts", "e2e/**/*.{ts,tsx}"], plugins: { regexp }, rules: { "regexp/no-super-linear-backtracking": "error", "regexp/no-super-linear-move": "error" } }`, following the file's existing block-comment style. Copy the `files:` glob idiom from the existing test-only block.
4. Run `pnpm exec eslint apps/edge apps/web apps/admin e2e` and save the complete violation list. This output is authoritative: fix every flagged regex, not just the candidates below. If it flags files beyond the table, they join the work (report the added files at the end).
5. Fix `apps/edge/src/routing.ts`: delete `const MODULE_PATH` and replace its test with linear string operations in the same function, e.g. `path.startsWith("/assets/") && path.endsWith(".br") && path.slice(8, -3).includes(".wasm-")`. Keep accept/reject behavior identical for all existing `routing.test.ts` cases.
6. Fix `apps/web/src/net/auth.ts`: (a) replace `SVG_PROLOG` with a scanner function `stripSvgProlog(text: string): string` that skips leading whitespace, one optional `<?xml …?>` (find the first `?>`), then loops stripping `<!--`…`-->` comments and `<!DOCTYPE`…`>` segments (scan the doctype honoring single/double quotes); (b) replace the data-URL regex with: case-insensitive `startsWith("data:image/svg+xml")` check, split parameters at the first `,`, validate each `;param` with a per-character loop over `[a-z0-9=-]` (lowercase the parameter first instead of the `i` flag), keep the after-comma remainder as the payload. Both must preserve existing `auth-methods.test.ts`/`auth.test.ts` outcomes exactly.
7. Fix `apps/web/src/net/roomLink.ts` only if flagged: replace the `text.match(...)` call with a scan for the literal prefixes `https://`, `http://`, `/play?room=`, `/together?coop=`, `/lobby/`, extending each candidate while the character is not in the terminator set (`\s"'<>`), then keep the existing trailing-punctuation strip and `URL`-based validation untouched.
8. Fix any remaining flagged regexes (likely test-only helpers, the `recipeText.ts` tokenizer, `i18n.ts`'s `TOKEN`). Never use `(?>…)` atomic groups or possessive quantifiers: JavaScript does not support them. Restructure with negated classes or plain string code. Never add `eslint-disable` comments for these two rules.
9. For each fixed regex, keep or extend the existing behavioral tests first (same accept/reject cases), then add the adversarial test from **Tests**.
10. Run the commands in **Tests** plus `pnpm exec eslint apps/edge apps/web apps/admin e2e` until all green. Record every decision the task did not settle with the rejected alternative.

## Tests

- `apps/edge/src/routing.test.ts`: add `it("module path check is linear on long adversarial input")` — feed `"/assets/" + "a".repeat(50_000)` (no `.wasm-`/`.br` tail, which trips the old double-`.*`) plus a 50k-char near-match containing many `.wasm-` fragments without trailing `.br`; assert the result is correct and `performance.now()` delta is under a file-local `const REDOS_BUDGET_MS = 1_000`, logging the actual ms.
- `apps/web/src/net/auth-methods.test.ts` (or `auth.test.ts`, per Step 3's grep): add `it("SVG prolog strip is linear on adversarial input")` — `"<!--" + "a".repeat(50_000)` (unclosed comment, the old nested-quantifier killer) and `"<?xml " + "a".repeat(50_000)`; and `it("SVG data-URL parse is linear on adversarial input")` — `"data:image/svg+xml" + ";a".repeat(25_000)` plus a 50k-char payload; same budget assertion.
- `apps/web/src/net/roomLink.test.ts` (only if fixed): add `it("findRoomLinkInText is linear on adversarial chat text")` — `"https://" + "a".repeat(50_000)` and `"/lobby/" + "!".repeat(50_000)`; assert null result and same budget.
- Any other fixed player-reachable regex: same shape of test in its colocated test file, with the adversarial string built to trip the OLD pattern (unclosed construct or near-match with repeated fragments).
- Commands: `pnpm exec eslint apps/edge apps/web e2e` (acceptance) and `pnpm exec eslint apps/edge apps/web apps/admin e2e` (rule scope); `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/net/roomLink.test.ts`, `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/net/auth-methods.test.ts` (or the touched auth test file); `pnpm exec vitest run --project edge`; root `pnpm typecheck` if any source signature changed.

## Done when

- [ ] `eslint-plugin-regexp` is a pinned root devDependency and both rules are errors over all four directories.
- [ ] `pnpm exec eslint apps/edge apps/web e2e` is green, and the wider four-directory run is green too.
- [ ] Every flagged regex is fixed with no `eslint-disable`, no atomic-group syntax, and unchanged accept/reject behavior on pre-existing tests.
- [ ] Every fixed regex on another player's text has its adversarial (~50k-char, millisecond-scale) test, each of which would time out or blow the budget against the old pattern.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web test` for each touched web test file and `pnpm exec vitest run --project edge` are green.
- [ ] No files outside the table (plus lint-flagged additions, reported) were changed; forbidden paths untouched.
- [ ] Decisions made beyond the task are recorded with rejected alternatives.

## Risks

- Behavior drift in the SVG prolog/data-URL parsers could accept a malicious avatar or reject a valid one: mitigated by running the pre-existing auth avatar tests unchanged and adding valid-input parity cases alongside the adversarial ones.
- `MODULE_PATH` semantics could widen/narrow which asset paths the Worker serves: mitigated by the existing `routing.test.ts` and `config.test.ts` (`run_worker_first` parity) cases passing unmodified.
- Timing assertions flaking on loaded CI: the 1,000 ms budget is ~100× above the expected few-ms linear cost but infinitely below exponential blowup, so it is robust; if CI proves otherwise, keep the assertion shape and raise only the constant with the observed numbers quoted.
- The plugin may flag many test-only regexes with no attacker reach: fix them genuinely (rewrite, not suppress) but add no adversarial tests for those.

## Open questions

- None blocking. Two things for a person at review, not the builder: the exact `eslint-plugin-regexp` version is whatever is latest when the builder runs the add command (recorded in the report); and per the issue, a new package plus `eslint.config.*` are review paths, so a person merges this one. If the plugin flags files far beyond the candidates above (a materially bigger item), the builder reports the list rather than silently expanding scope past ~40 files.
